Pen-test finding (severity: high) against the product media endpoint.

With `MEDIA_ROOT=/srv/shop/media`, the testers requested

    GET /media/..%2Fmedia-backups%2Fcustomers.csv

and got back the customer export that lives in `/srv/shop/media-backups/`, a directory
next to the media folder. The obvious `..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd` style requests are
refused with a 404, so some containment check exists but it doesn't hold up. Nothing
outside the media root may be served, whatever the encoding. Nested paths inside the
root (e.g. `thumbs%2Ftee.png`) still have to work.

setup.create:
"""Product media (photos, size charts) served from ``config.MEDIA_ROOT``.

``GET /media/{name}`` serves one file below the media root. Clients
URL-encode ``name``, so ``thumbs%2Ftee.png`` addresses
``<MEDIA_ROOT>/thumbs/tee.png``.
"""

import mimetypes
import os
from urllib.parse import unquote

from shop import config
from shop.errors import NotFound


def media_root() -> str:
    return os.path.abspath(config.MEDIA_ROOT)


def resolve_media_path(name: str) -> str:
    """Absolute path of the media file addressed by ``name`` (URL-encoded)."""
    root = media_root()
    candidate = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(root, unquote(name)))
    if not candidate.startswith(root):
        raise NotFound(f"media {name} not found")
    return candidate


def get_media(ctx, request, name):
    path = resolve_media_path(name)
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        raise NotFound(f"media {name} not found")
    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
        data = handle.read()
    content_type = mimetypes.guess_type(path)[0] or "application/octet-stream"
    return {"status": 200, "headers": {"Content-Type": content_type}, "body": data}
